$comment: The scripting contract shared by the C# Jint bridge (SexyBiscuit.Engine/Scripting/ScriptBridge.cs) and the browser bridge (html5/src/scripting/ScriptBridge.js). A test on each side pins its bridge to the member names here, so adding a member without adding it to both bridges fails both suites; shared=false marks a member one engine has and the other does not, and the validator warns when a script uses one. The other fields describe each member for tools: a fn has params (name, type, optional, variadic) and returns; a prop has type and readonly; both may carry doc and since (1 when absent). Types are TypeScript type expressions carried verbatim. `types` declares the helper interfaces those types name; `meta` documents the globals and names the interface each section becomes. html5/tools/gen-dts.js writes sb-engine.d.ts from this file, the C# assembly embeds that, and `npm run lint` fails when the checked-in file is stale. Never edit the .d.ts by hand.

id.doc: Stable numeric id, unique within the running scene.

tag.doc: Tag string used for collision filtering and scene queries.

active.doc: Whether this actor is active and updated each frame.

transform.doc: The same object as the `transform` global.

transform3d.doc: The actor's Transform3D, or null in a 2D scene.

getComponent.doc: The first component of the named type, or null.

addComponent.doc: Adds a component by type name and returns its proxy.

destroy.doc: Remove this actor from the scene at the end of the current frame.

parent.doc: The actor this one is attached to, or null at the root.

children.doc: A fresh array of the actors attached to this one.

attachTo.doc: Parents this actor to another; null detaches. keep (default true) holds the world position, so a pickup follows the player from where it is rather than snapping to the player's origin.

detach.doc: Removes this actor from its parent, keeping its world position by default.

findChild.doc: The first child with this name, or null; recursive searches the whole subtree.

lookAt.doc: Rotates the actor so it faces the point (x, y) in world space.

distanceTo.doc: The distance from this transform to another {x, y}.

scaleX.doc: Local scale on X. Every mesh primitive is unit-sized, so scale is how a cube becomes a wall.

set.doc: Position and scale in one call: one matrix rebuild instead of six.

isPressed.doc: True on the frame the named action becomes active.

isHeld.doc: True while the named action is active.

isReleased.doc: True on the frame the named action stops being active.

getAxis.doc: The axis value for the named action, -1..1.

mouseX.doc: Mouse cursor X in screen pixels.

mouseY.doc: Mouse cursor Y in screen pixels.

mouseDeltaX.doc: Mouse movement since the last frame.

scrollDelta.doc: Scroll wheel movement since the last frame, in notches.

isKeyDown.doc: Keys by name: "A", "a", "KeyA", "Space", "ArrowLeft" and "Left" all work.

isMouseDown.doc: Mouse buttons: 0 left, 1 middle, 2 right, or "Left" / "Middle" / "Right".

getTouch.returns: { id: number; x: number; y: number; phase: string } | null

joystickX.doc: The left on-screen joystick, -1..1 on each axis.

play.doc: Starts playback and returns a handle; id is 0 when nothing could play.

stop.doc: Stops the voice behind a handle (or a raw id).

name.doc: The name of the scene this actor is in.

find.doc: The first actor with the given name, or null.

findAll.doc: Every actor with the given name.

findByTag.doc: Every actor with the given tag. An empty array is still truthy.

findFirstByTag.doc: The first actor with the given tag, or null.

createActor.doc: Creates an empty actor in this scene at (x, y).

addComponent.doc: Adds a component to an actor by type name, applying {Property: value} pairs.

destroy.doc: Removes an actor at the end of the frame.

instantiate.doc: Instantiates a prefab file at (x, y), or an empty actor named after the path.

load.doc: Requests a scene transition at the end of the frame.

log.doc: Writes an informational message. Arguments are joined with spaces.

normalize.doc: The unit vector, or {x: 0, y: 0} for a zero vector.

raycast.returns: { actor: ActorProxy; x: number; y: number; normalX: number; normalY: number; distance: number } | null
raycast.doc: The closest hit along a ray, or null.

overlapCircle.doc: Every actor whose collider overlaps the circle.

overlapBox.doc: Every actor whose collider overlaps the axis-aligned box.

time.doc: Scaled seconds since the engine started.

timeScale.doc: 0 pauses gameplay, 0.5 is slow motion, 2 is double speed.

connect.doc: Joins a server by address and port, or a relay by ws:// URL and room code.

isHost.doc: True when this session hosts the game: the server, or the solo player.

ping.doc: Round-trip time to the server in milliseconds; 0 when not connected.

room.doc: The room code of a session joined through a relay, or an empty string.

playerName.doc: The name other players see. Set it before connecting.

players.doc: A fresh array of the players in the session.

startSolo.doc: Starts a single-player session that satisfies isHost and isConnected, so a multiplayer script runs alone.

sendTo.doc: Sends a message to one player.

on.doc: Subscribes to a session event and returns the function that unsubscribes. Needs a running session; the onNetworkMessage hook waits for one instead.

safeLeft.doc: What a notch or a television's overscan leaves usable.

build.doc: Builds a whole tree in one call and returns its root. Building again replaces it.

find.doc: The first node with this name, or null.

clear.doc: Drops this script's nodes. Another script's HUD is untouched.

measure.doc: The width one line of text will occupy.

order.doc: Paint order against the canvases other scripts own. Higher is in front.

focused.doc: The node holding focus, or null.

setFocus.doc: Moves focus to a node, or to the node with that name.

navigate.doc: Steps focus one place. Returns whether anything moved.

inputMode.doc: Which class of device the player is driving with.

space.doc: Whether this script's canvas is a surface on the screen or a plane in the world.

facing.doc: How a world-space canvas turns to face the player.

worldX.doc: Where a world canvas stands, when the script's actor has no 3D transform.

pixelsPerUnit.doc: Canvas units per world unit: the size dial for a world canvas.

available.doc: True when the build carries the Darks Games account layer. Every DG member is safe to call without it.

signedIn.doc: True once the player has signed in.

userId.doc: The account id, or null when signed out.

userName.doc: The account name, or null when signed out.

handle.doc: The public handle, or null when signed out.

displayName.doc: The name to show; "Player" when signed out.

game.doc: The catalogue slug this build was exported with, or an empty string.

presence.doc: Publishes what the player is doing, e.g. { state: 'lobby', joinCode: room }.

achievement.doc: Reports an achievement, or adds to a counted one.

loadSave.doc: Requests the cloud save. It arrives on the "save" event rather than as a return value, because the Jint bridge cannot await.

on.doc: Subscribes to an account event and returns the function that unsubscribes. "user" reports (signedIn, id, displayName) on both engines.

spawn.doc: Spawns a character from a `.chibi` recipe under Assets/. The recipe is read from disk, so the body appears a frame or two later; the actor itself is usable at once.

random.doc: A coordinated random character. The same seed is always the same character.

play.doc: Plays a clip, cross-fading over `blend` seconds. Locomotion: "idle", "walk", "run". Keyed: "wave", "hit", "jump", "cheer", "sit", "die". False for a name that is neither.

stop.doc: Stops whatever is playing, returning the character to rest.

setColour.doc: Repaints one colour slot: skin, hair, eyes, top, bottom, shoes, accent.

setStyle.doc: Swaps one style slot — head, hair, eyes, body, legs, feet — and rebuilds.

attach.doc: Hangs an actor off a socket: Head, Face, Hand_L, Hand_R, Back.

socket.doc: The socket's own actor, for reading where it is. Null for an unknown name.

transform.doc: Position and rotation of the found actor.

transform3d.doc: The actor's Transform3D, or null in a 2D scene.

onAwake.doc: Called once when the script loads, after the actor has joined its scene.

onStart.doc: Called once on the first frame after the scene has started.

onUpdate.doc: Called every frame. `dt` is seconds since the last frame.

onFixedUpdate.doc: Called at a fixed rate regardless of frame rate. Use for physics-dependent logic.

onLateUpdate.doc: Called every frame after every onUpdate has run.

onDestroy.doc: Called just before the actor is destroyed or the scene unloads.

onCollisionEnter.doc: Called when this actor's collider first contacts another collider.

onCollisionStay.doc: Called every physics step while the contact persists.

onTriggerEnter.doc: Called when another collider enters this actor's trigger volume.

onTriggerStay.doc: Called every physics step while it stays inside.

onNetworkMessage.doc: Called for every message the session delivers. Defining it is enough: the script attaches itself the frame a session appears.

worldFollow.doc: Whether this node chases worldAnchor across the screen. Following owns the node's positioning, offset and visibility.

worldAnchor.doc: The point in the world a following node tracks, as [x, y, z].

worldFollowDistance.doc: Stop showing a following node past this distance. Zero never stops.

rect.type: { x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number }

parent.doc: The node this one hangs under, or null at the root.

children.doc: A fresh array each read, so a script cannot mutate the tree by writing to it.

add.doc: Appends a child built from a spec and returns it.

find.doc: The first descendant with this name, or null.

remove.doc: Detaches this node and everything under it.

focus.doc: Gives this node the focus a pad or a remote drives.

Vec2.doc: Plain {x, y} value object used throughout the API.

AudioHandle.doc: Opaque handle returned by Audio.play(). Pass it to Audio.stop() to halt playback.

ComponentProxy.doc: A component reached through getComponent(). Every schema-declared property is readable and writable under its C# name and its camelCase name ("GravityScale" or "gravityScale"); vectors read as {x, y} and colours as "#RRGGBBAA".

ScriptProxy.doc: A ScriptComponent seen from another script.

invoke.doc: Calls a top-level function the other script defines and returns its result.

actor.doc: The Actor that owns this script component.

transform3d.doc: The actor's Transform3D, or null in a 2D scene. Rotations are Euler angles in degrees.

Input.doc: Input queries: actions, keys, mouse, touch and the on-screen joystick.

Vector2.doc: 2D vector maths over plain {x, y} objects.

Network.doc: The multiplayer session. Present in every build so a multiplayer script runs solo; a solo session satisfies every query.

UI.doc: The screen, and the tree a script builds on it -- or a plane standing in the world, when `space` says so. The only global that knows how big the window is.

DG.doc: Darks Games accounts and social: identity, presence, achievements and cloud saves. Every member is safe to call in a build without the layer.

Chibi.doc: MakeChibi's characters: spawning, dressing and animating them.

actorProxy.doc: An actor found through the Scene API, a hierarchy query or a collision.

actorProxyTransform.doc: The transform of a found actor: position and rotation only.

collisionData.doc: Contact data handed to the collision hooks. tag, name and getComponent forward to `other`.

uiNode.doc: One node in the tree, as UI.build returns it. The members are generated from UiDocument's own key list on both engines, so this and the contract cannot describe different things.
